primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.

primary_source.headline: From Gulshan Kumar to Tiger Shroff, Bollywood figures in the crosshairs
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Actor Tiger Shroff, who escaped unhurt after three rounds were fired at him in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday, is the latest Bollywood personality to have been the target of shootings over the years.In February this year, five rounds were fired outside the Juhu residence of filmmaker Rohit Shetty. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing.In April 2024, two bike-borne men fired five rounds outside actor Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai’s Bandra area.The Mumbai Police arrested many suspects linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. A trial against the five accused - Vicky Gupta, Sagar Pal, Harpal Singh, Sonukumar Bishnoi, and Mohammad Rafiq Choudhari - is underway. The sixth accused, Anuj Kumar Thapan, died in police custody in May 2024.In January 2000, filmmaker Rakesh Roshan was shot and injured in an assassination attempt in Santacruz area of Mumbai, just a week after the release of his blockbuster film Kaho Naa Pyaar Hai.Tiger Shroff escapes unhurt as suspected Lawrence Bishnoi gang members open fireTwo assailants fired multiple shots at him. One bullet hit his left arm and another grazed his chest.In August 1997, T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar was shot dead outside the Jiteshwar Mahadev Temple in Mumbai’s Andheri area. He was shot 16 times by the assailants.Comedian Kapil Sharma's restaurant, Kap's Café, located in Canada’s British Columbia province, was targeted in three separate shooting incidents between July and October last year.

primary_source.headline: Less plastic, more pujo vibes: Assam town gives Durga Puja a 'carbon-neutral' twist
primary_source.content: Durga Puja celebrations mean glitzy pandals, excessive lighting, high-decibel music and many more attractions.But several committees organising the annual Durga Puja in Kokrajhar town in western Assam, the district headquarters of the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), have pitched in to adopt the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations by planting trees, reducing the use of non-biodegradable items and even lowering the volume of music systems to check sound pollution.A set of dos and don'ts were proposed by the Kokrajhar district administration for nearly 200 Durga Puja committees in the town as part of efforts to popularise the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations.“We proposed the idea as part of our efforts to have environmentally responsible festivities while preserving the religious and cultural essence of the festival. It is very nice to see that nearly 50 per cent of the committees have responded very positively by significantly reducing the use of plastic items, planting trees and even controlling the volume of music systems,” Kokrajhar District Commissioner Pankaj Chakravarty told DH over the phone on Sunday. Kokrajhar is situated about 200 km west of Guwahati.Durga Puja celebrations began on Friday and will continue till Wednesday, following which the Durga idols will be immersed in rivers.With a population of nearly 35,000 (2011 Census), Kokrajhar Municipal town has diverse communities, including Bodos, Bengalis, Assamese, Rabhas, Nepalis, Adivasis, Saranias and others, each peacefully celebrating their own festivals.Lotus theme, red-and-white decor to mark Durga Puja in BengaluruCarbon-neutral celebrationsUnder the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations, the district administration proposed several measures, such as encouraging the use of locally available and reusable materials, including bamboo, jute, recycled paper and other environmentally responsible alternatives, for pandals and decorations; promoting idols made from natural clay and other biodegradable materials, with non-toxic colours, to minimise environmental pollution, particularly during immersion; tree plantation; the use of solar energy and LED lights; responsible sound management; and encouraging waste segregation, responsible disposal and recycling, among other measures.“This is an encouraging beginning. The drive is resulting in public awareness, with the concept being shared by many on social media platforms. We hope more and more Durga Puja committees will accept and implement the concept gradually in the years ahead to make environmental awareness an integral part of the festivities, encouraging every puja committee and community to contribute towards a cleaner and greener Kokrajhar and Assam at large,” Chakravarty said.“The message is simple: let our devotion to Maa Durga inspire us to protect Mother Earth. Through collective efforts by puja committees, citizens, community organisations and the District Administration, Kokrajhar aspires to set a meaningful example of how faith, tradition and sustainability can go hand in hand, contributing to a greener future for the Bodoland Territorial Region and Assam as a whole.”

primary_source.headline: Reports of sale false and misleading, says Bhilai Steel Plant amid Congress alleging Adani visit
primary_source.content: Durg: Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP), a Chhattisgarh-based unit of state-run Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), on Sunday dismissed reports about its proposed sale as "false and misleading", the assertion coming amid allegations from the Congress that the Adani Group was planning to visit the facility.The BSP is located in Bhilai city in Durg district.In a statement, the BSP said the Ministry of Steel has refuted the claims through its official social media handle, while the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check had also confirmed that the reports are false.The plant appealed to its employees, stakeholders and the people of Chhattisgarh not to believe or circulate unverified information and urged them to rely on official and authenticated sources."BSP is not merely an industrial establishment; it is an integral part of Chhattisgarh's identity, pride and industrial legacy. Since its inception, the plant has played a pivotal role in the state's industrial development by generating employment, supporting ancillary industries and contributing to the livelihoods of thousands of families," it said.Its legacy and contribution have made it a source of pride for the people of Chhattisgarh, the statement asserted.Karnataka government to negotiate with Adani over tunnel road costAs a major unit of SAIL, the Bhilai Steel Plant continues to contribute to the growth of the country's steel sector and strengthen India's industrial capabilities, the statement said.The BSP urged the people to refrain from spreading misinformation that could create unnecessary confusion among employees, their families and the people of Chhattisgarh.The clarification came after former Chhattisgarh chief minister and senior Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel alleged that Adani was likely to visit the plant.In a post on X on October 14, Baghel said, "It has come to light that Adani is set to visit the Bhilai Steel Plant - our BSP. Do you understand the implications of Adani's visit to the BSP? It means that Narendra Modi who is spearheading a campaign to sell off the nation, has now set his sights on our BSP. And his favored buyer is coming to conduct an inspection"."Modi ji should realize that the BSP is the soul of Chhattisgarh. And we, the people of Chhattisgarh, will not allow it to be sold under any circumstances. Not under any circumstances," Baghel added.Chhattisgarh BJP leaders should also understand that BSP is not for sale, Baghel had said.Meanwhile, Congress's Bhilai unit president Mukesh Chandrakar, in a statement on Sunday, said reports about the plant's possible privatisation and the Adani Group's alleged visit had triggered anger in the industrial town.The reports had created apprehensions among employees, local shopkeepers and residents over job security, minimum wages for workers and the future of the plant's township, he claimed.
